analysis.summary: Rust 2024 tail-expression drop-order migration bug fix: BID hints must be scheduled for all tail temporaries, not only those with significant drop, so borrowck can detect borrows that would become invalid at the future drop location. The patch also avoids an opaque-normalization query cycle in the tail_expr_drop_order lint by using a non-body-analysis typing environment. ElaborateDrops MIR fixtures record the newly retained BID statement.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this fix, `schedule_backwards_incompatible_drop` returned early for temporaries whose types lacked a significant destructor: `if !self.local_decls[local].ty.has_significant_drop(self.tcx, self.typing_env()) { return; }`. Borrowck also ignored every BID hint as irrelevant to borrow checking (`StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint { .. }` was in the no-op arm), so possible borrow-checking failures at the Rust 2024 future drop location were not diagnosed. Separately, the tail-expression lint built its typing environment with `ty::TypingEnv::post_analysis(tcx, def_id)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was the early-return gate that dropped BID scheduling for temporaries without significant drop: `if !self.local_decls[local].ty.has_significant_drop(self.tcx, self.typing_env()) { return; }`. That caused ElaborateDrops output to omit a BID hint for such a temporary; the patch removes the gate so the fixture now contains `backward incompatible drop(_4);` in addition to the existing `backward incompatible drop(_2);` and `backward incompatible drop(_5);`. With BIDs retained, borrowck checks live borrows at the Edition2024 backward-incompatible drop and emits `tail_expr_drop_order` when a conflict exists. The lint's typing environment was also changed from post-analysis to `ty::TypingEnv::non_body_analysis(tcx, def_id)` to avoid a normalization cycle for local opaques such as a recursively boxed future.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source compiled in Edition 2021 for Rust 2024 migration, especially tail-expression temporaries whose drop scope changes in Edition 2024 and that have a borrow still live at the future drop location. Includes temporaries that do not need `Drop`, such as `&str` borrowed from a temporary `String`, references to temporaries in unsafe blocks, references to closures, and Copy temporaries. Also includes async functions whose tail-expression lint normalizes local opaque types, e.g. `Box::pin(test()).await?`, and thread-local/shared-reference cases where the borrowed type does not need Drop.
analysis.trigger: A `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` with `BackwardIncompatibleDropReason::Edition2024` is reached while a borrow involving the hinted place is still in scope, or the tail_expr_drop_order lint normalizes a recursive local opaque type. The hint is associated with a temporary whose drop order changes under Rust 2024, and the type may or may not need `Drop`.
preconditions: The crate uses Edition 2021 while enabling or denying the Rust 2024 `tail_expr_drop_order` lint; the regression test uses `//@ edition: 2021` and `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`.
A backward-incompatible drop hint is emitted for an Edition2024 tail-expression temporary; BID scheduling must not be gated on `has_significant_drop`.
At least one non-fake borrow involving the BID place must still be live in the borrowck state at that location, using either Polonius output or `state.borrows`.

If the hinted type does not need `Drop`, the access depth must be `AccessDepth::Shallow(None)`, not `AccessDepth::Drop`, because borrows behind shared references such as thread locals are not tracked.
For recursive opaque types, the lint must use `ty::TypingEnv::non_body_analysis(tcx, def_id)` rather than `post_analysis` to avoid an opaque-normalization query cycle.
pitfalls: Gating BID scheduling on `has_significant_drop` misses borrowck violations at future drop locations; the patch explicitly says `We need to know all of them so that we can capture potential borrow-checking errors.`

Treating every BID as `AccessDepth::Drop` is wrong when the type does not need Drop; the patch says this would `ICE because we don't track borrows behind shared references.` Use `Shallow(None)` in that case.
Do not report fake borrows; `check_backward_incompatible_drop` skips `BorrowKind::Fake(_)`.
Stop after the first violation in this simplified check (`// We may stop at the first case` / `Control::Break`).

Borrows in scope must be computed with the same Polonius-vs-non-Polonius logic as normal borrowck; the patch extracts `borrows_in_scope` and uses `Cow` to return either `polonius.errors_at(location)` or `state.borrows`.

Using `post_analysis` for the tail_expr_drop_order typing environment can produce a cycle error when normalizing recursive opaque types; the new regression test is a check-pass test for `Box::pin(test()).await?`.
A BID statement is a lint hint in MIR, not the actual drop; the ElaborateDrops fixture change only records that the hint is now retained for the additional place.
analysis.testStrategy: Add Edition 2021 UI tests under `tests/ui/drop` with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]` that exercise borrows live across Rust 2024 tail-expression temporaries: `let _ = { String::new().as_str() }.len();`, `f(unsafe { String::new().as_str() }.len());`, `f({ &mut || 0 })`, and the Copy temporary case `g({ &f() });`. Assert the lint label `this temporary value will be dropped at the end of the block`, the borrow explanation, and the Edition 2024 warning. Check both panic-abort and panic-unwind ElaborateDrops MIR fixtures now include `backward incompatible drop(_4);` alongside `_2` and `_5`. Add a check-pass recursive boxed-future test (`Box::pin(test()).await?`) to ensure no normalize cycle, and a check-pass thread-local/shared-reference test to ensure no ICE when the BID type does not need Drop.
